ranking.note: Raised to P1: a confirmed data race (issue 36515) in the Mining IPC that external template providers hit is a reliability/correctness defect, which outranks the feature work sharing P2.
Kept P2 but placed first among them: it introduces the BlockTemplateManager that #33922, #36356 and #36357 build on, so it gates several other listed PRs.
Moved up: signed-overflow UB that silently drops prioritised transactions from templates is a template-correctness issue, ranking above tooling and ergonomics P3s even though it is hard to trigger.
Lowered to P4 and moved down: reviewers confirm the no-mempool lookup path is unreachable in production, making it narrower than the other P3 bug fixes.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain: #35581 adds BlockTemplateManager; #36356 moves the getblocktemplate cache into it, #36357 is explicitly based on #36356, and #33922 tracks templates through it. Review order should be #35581 → #36356 → #36357, with #33922 after #35581.

#36525 (mutex around m_block_template, WaitAndCreateNewBlock refactor) and #35581 (template lifecycle moved into BlockTemplateManager) touch the same template ownership/locking code; the race fix should be reviewed first so the manager refactor is rebased onto correct locking rather than the reverse.

#36525 (getTotalFees), #33922 (getMemoryLoad), #35300 (precious arg, which deprecates existing capnp ordinals) and #36097 (replaces interrupt methods with cancellation arguments) all modify the same Mining capnp interface; the ordinal/compat decisions in #35300 and #36097 should be settled before the two additive getters land to avoid repeated client-breaking churn.

#36357's user-visible payoff (getmininginfo no longer reporting fee-estimator templates) sits behind the pure refactor #36356, so #36356 inherits review urgency from it despite being the less consequential change on its own.

#36367 is labelled mempool but is ranked here because its only stated symptom is getblocktemplate omitting prioritised transactions; if the mempool category also carries it, dedupe there rather than here.
#30437 and #36791 both touch the IPC mining functional test harness; #36791's timeout/monotonic-clock fix is small and should not be blocked on the larger bitcoin-mine test program.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: one confirmed correctness/race defect (P1), four substantial Mining-interface capabilities aimed at Stratum v2 consumers (P2), a band of genuine but deferrable bug fixes, refactors and tooling (P3), and two narrow/theoretical cleanups (P4). Per the category guidance, #36156's exact-limit underfill fix is kept low because the fee upside is a negligible fraction of a block.
